headline: Clean Energy Finally Meets All New Global Electricity Demand
meta_description: For the first time, rising global electricity needs were fully covered by renewable power rather than fossil fuels, marking a turning point in the energy trans…
summary_short: Renewable energy has grown fast enough to meet all new global electricity demand for the first time ever, as solar overtakes coal in the global mix.
body:
For the first time ever, rising electricity needs were fully covered by clean power rather than fossil fuels. This milestone signals that the world's energy transition is not only happening—it's accelerating.

The shift is most striking in the world's two largest economies. China and India, traditionally the biggest drivers of fossil-fuel growth, both saw declines in fossil generation thanks to record renewable expansion. The change ripples through the global energy mix: solar has now overtaken coal as a source of electricity worldwide.

What makes this moment significant is not just one achievement, but the convergence of multiple trends. Renewable energy is growing faster than electricity demand itself. The two nations most responsible for historical coal expansion are now leading the charge toward clean power. These interlocking changes suggest the energy transition has reached a critical tipping point—no longer a marginal shift, but the new direction of global growth.
quick_facts: First time: all new global electricity demand met by renewables
China and India: both reduced fossil fuel generation
Solar has overtaken coal in the global electricity mix
